chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man dies leaving his wife and he has not yet entered into her (consummated the marriage), then she is entitled to the full dowry if a specific dowry was designated for her, and her dowry is part of the inheritance. And if no specific dowry was designated for her, she is not entitled to a specific dowry, but she is entitled to the inheritance.
ai.seo_question: What are the wife's financial rights if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between the dowry (mahr) and inheritance shares for a wife whose husband dies before consummation, emphasizing that the mahr is a debt on the estate rather than a portion of the inheritance itself. Shia jurists utilize this hadith to resolve potential conflicts in inheritance calculations, ensuring the wife receives her full agreed or standard mahr prior to the distribution of the remaining estate. This ruling highlights the practical application of marital financial rights in early Shia legal theory as compiled by Shaykh al-Tusi.
